   is clipped at each panel's edges instead of forming one continuous frame. instruction.md gives
   only the user-visible symptom via the screenshot - no file, component, CSS class, layer

   must recognise this as an occlusion/layering defect from the image alone, then find the
   follow-indicator render on its own. The fix is conceptually non-trivial even once found:
   raising the indicator's z-index cannot work, because it renders inside a container whose own
   stacking context is capped below the UI layer's, and a child's z-index can never escape its
   ancestor's stacking context. The only fix that works is relocating the indicator's render out
   of the canvas-overlay component and into the UI-layer component, placed after the panel groups
   so ordinary paint order puts it on top, and kept there in every layout including the
   minimal/focus layout where the usual panels are swapped out.

   solution/fix.patch): a single comparison operator is flipped in Editor.ts's
   getViewportPageBoundsForFollowing (`<` -> `>`), inverting the branch that grows our viewport to
   fully contain the followed user's viewport while preserving our own aspect ratio. Whenever the
   two users' aspect ratios differ, the follower's target viewport is undersized instead of
   correctly enlarged, and the camera ends up over-zoomed relative to what the leader is actually
   showing. Not part of the described bug and has no dedicated repo tests before this task (the
   whole describe block was `it.todo`); requires deriving the correct "smallest box of a given
   aspect ratio that contains another box" geometry to notice the sign is backwards.

3. Hidden, injected via environment/assets/bugs/bug_02.patch (applied to harbor_base, reversed in
   solution/fix.patch): in the same startFollowingUser method, a few hundred lines away, the page-
   follow effect's condition is inverted (`!==` -> `===`), so it "switches page" precisely when the
   leader's page already matches ours (a no-op) and does nothing when the leader actually navigates
   to a different page - silently breaking cross-page following. Also has no dedicated test before
   this task; the fix requires noticing that the visible condition contradicts its own comment
   ("if the page changed, switch page") once read carefully, not any signal from outside the code.

Both hidden bugs live in the same method/feature area as each other (startFollowingUser) but are
functionally and spatially independent of the disclosed CSS/DOM bug - a narrow fix informed only by
the screenshot would never open Editor.ts at all. The closing instruction line is what makes
looking there a legitimate, motivated choice rather than a lucky guess; actually finding and fixing
each bug still requires reading unfamiliar, untested reactive/geometry code with no external cue

FROM node:22-bookworm

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    git ca-certificates curl python3 build-essential \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Enable corepack for Yarn 4 Berry (tldraw uses yarn4 + workspaces)
RUN corepack enable

WORKDIR /app

# [IMPORTANT] Copy bug patches to a TEMP path (not into /app) so they can be applied
# into the base snapshot below and never reach the agent-visible tree.
COPY assets/bugs/ /tmp/bugs/

# Clone, pin to base commit, strip .git (anti-cheat: agent cannot see fix PR history).
# Re-init a single-commit repo tagged harbor_base so the verifier can reset test files.
RUN git clone https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw /app \
 && git -C /app checkout 56c3bc3fbec3bdf48e314732a51dd22fcfdd53a5 \
 && rm -rf /app/.git \
 # [IMPORTANT] Apply every bug patch BEFORE the snapshot below, so each defect
 # becomes part of harbor_base (the exact state the agent starts from).
 && for p in /tmp/bugs/*.patch; do git -C /app apply "$p" || patch -p1 -d /app < "$p"; done \
 && git -C /app init -q \
 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h add -A \
 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h commit -q -m base \
 # [IMPORTANT] harbor_base = base commit + all bug patches. Must come AFTER the
 # apply loop; the verifier resets to this tag.
 && git -C /app tag harbor_base

# Pre-install workspace dependencies (pinned lockfile)
RUN yarn install --immutable 2>&1 | tail -10 || yarn install 2>&1 | tail -10

# Visual evidence readable by the agent at /app/.harbor_assets/
# tests/ and solution/ are NOT baked in — supplied by the harness at verify time
RUN mkdir -p /logs /app/.harbor_assets
COPY assets/ /app/.harbor_assets/
# [IMPORTANT] Delete the bug diffs from the agent-visible dir so the agent can't read
# the answer (the reverse of a bug patch is the fix), and drop the authoring-only
# asset manifest, which describes the screenshot's defect in prose the task must not
# leak to the agent (the image itself stays — it's the one thing meant to be read).
RUN rm -rf /app/.harbor_assets/bugs /app/.harbor_assets/ASSET_MANIFEST.json

CMD ["bash"]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Behavioral verifier for tldraw__tldraw-8821-mm
# "Following indicator border is hidden behind menus and panels" (PR #9210 / issue #8821)
#
# Applies the PR's test additions, runs vitest jsdom + RTL tests in @tldraw/tldraw,
# and computes a reward from the JUnit XML report.
# NEVER greps source for the fix — it runs the tests.
set -uo pipefail
mkdir -p /logs/verifier
STDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt
STDERR_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stderr.txt
REPORT=/logs/verifier/report.xml
: > "$STDOUT_LOG"; : > "$STDERR_LOG"

ensure_reward() { [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt; }
trap ensure_reward EXIT

cd /app || { echo "no /app" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# ── Reset test files the agent may have touched ─────────────────────────────
# Restore every path mentioned in test.patch to the pristine harbor_base state
# BEFORE applying test.patch, so agent edits to tests cannot affect scoring.
# The agent's source fix (in the non-test files) is preserved.
# NOTE: clean the exact paths test.patch owns, never their parent directory —
# a dirname-wide `git clean` would also delete a legitimate off-file
# alternative's own new source file if it happens to land beside a test file.
_patch_paths=$(grep '^+++ b/' /tests/test.patch | sed 's#^+++ b/##')
for _p in $_patch_paths; do
  git checkout harbor_base -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null \
    || rm -f "/app/$_p" 2>/dev/null || true
done
git clean -fdq -- $_patch_paths 2>/dev/null || true

echo "== applying test.patch ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
git apply --binary /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || git apply /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || patch -p1 -i /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: could not apply test.patch" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

echo "== installing pinned test-only deps (none extra; vitest + RTL are in the lockfile) ==" \
  | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
# @testing-library/react, @testing-library/dom and vitest are already in yarn.lock
# (packages/tldraw's own devDependencies). No extra install step needed.

echo "== running f2p + p2p tests ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
# f2p: "places the following indicator inside the UI layout, not the canvas-in-front overlay"
#      "renders the following indicator after the toolbar and menu panels in the UI layout"
#      "still places the following indicator inside the UI layout while in focus mode"
#      "expands the viewport to fully contain the followed user, preserving our own aspect ratio"
#      "follows a user to another page without unfollowing them"
# p2p: "still renders the rich text toolbar inside the canvas-in-front overlay"
#      "still renders the image toolbar inside the canvas-in-front overlay"
#      "still renders the video toolbar inside the canvas-in-front overlay"
#      "still renders the cursor chat bubble inside the canvas-in-front overlay"
#      "renders no following indicator when no override is supplied and nobody is being followed"
#      "renders the following indicator override exactly once"

# all-it.todo) viewport-following.test.ts. Run both; vitest only executes the matched files.
cd /app/packages/tldraw
yarn run -T vitest run \
  --reporter=junit --outputFile="$REPORT" \
  "src/test/ui/FollowingIndicatorLayering" \
  "src/test/viewport-following" \
  >>"$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || echo "(vitest exited non-zero; parsing report anyway)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

# Rubric judge - SUB-AGENT backend: no API key, no network. On the first pass there is no
# verdict yet, so judge.py writes a judge request under /logs/verifier/judge/ and prints
# nothing. The `|| echo ""` is load-bearing: the judge must never be able to fail the run.
RUBRIC=""
if [ -f /tests/rubrics.json ]; then
  RUBRIC=$(python3 /tests/judge.py --rubrics /tests/rubrics.json --repo /app \

fi

python3 /tests/verifier.py --rubric "${RUBRIC:-}" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
echo "reward=$(cat /logs/verifier/reward.txt 2>/dev/null)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Reward verifier for tldraw__tldraw-8821-mm
"Following indicator border is hidden behind menus and panels" (PR #9210 / issue #8821)

Parses the JUnit XML produced by vitest and computes a BINARY reward:
  1.0 — all f2p pass AND all p2p pass
  0.0 — anything else: a strict subset of f2p passing, a p2p regression,
        or a suite that failed to run. There is no partial credit; the
        f2p_passed / p2p_passed counts carry how close a run got.

f2p (fail-to-pass): tests that FAIL on base, PASS after fix. Three defects are covered, all within
    "the follow experience" but only one disclosed by mechanism in instruction.md (the closing line
    tells the agent there is more than one, without saying what or where) - see task.toml's
    difficulty_explanation:
      - the FollowingIndicator slot renders inside the UI layout's own stacking context
        (.tlui-layout), after the panel groups, instead of inside the canvas's lower-stacking-
        context overlay (.tl-canvas__in-front) where panels always painted over it - including the
        focus-mode branch, which swaps out the panel chrome but must not swap out the follow
        border along with it (disclosed, image-gated);
      - the camera-follow viewport-fit math in Editor.ts correctly grows to contain the followed
        user's viewport across mismatched aspect ratios (undisclosed by mechanism);
      - the page-follow effect in the same Editor.ts method switches the follower's page when the
        leader actually navigates elsewhere, instead of only when their page already matches ours
        (undisclosed by mechanism).
p2p (pass-to-pass): tests that PASS on both base and fix. These guard against regressions to the
    sibling in-front-of-canvas slots (rich text/image/video toolbars, cursor chat bubble) that the
    disclosed fix's diff also touches, and against the fix accidentally rendering the indicator when
    nobody is being followed or rendering it more than once.

BEHAVIORAL CONTRACT: reward is derived entirely from the test report.
This verifier NEVER inspects source code for the fix string or any other token.
"""
import json, os, re, sys, xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

CONF       = json.load(open('/tests/config.json'))
F2P        = CONF['f2p']
P2P        = CONF['p2p']
REPORT     = '/logs/verifier/report.xml'


# ── Canonical reward writer + --rubric gate ──────────────────────────────────
# reward.json MUST be a FLAT map of numbers with exactly these seven keys: harbor parses
# it as VerifierResult.rewards and PREFERS it over reward.txt. A nested dict, list or
# string raises a ValidationError that aborts the trial before any reward is recorded —
# while reward.txt still gets written in-container, so the run looks scored when harbor
# stored nothing. Registered with atexit so it writes last.
import atexit

_CANON_JSON = '/logs/verifier/reward.json'
_CANON_TXT  = '/logs/verifier/reward.txt'
_canon = {}


def canon_reward(f2p_passed, f2p_total, p2p_passed, p2p_total, rubric):
    """THE reward policy. BINARY — there is no partial credit.

    tests_passed is 1.0 only when every f2p test passes AND every p2p test still passes.
    A strict subset of f2p passing is not partial progress worth scoring: the task is
    unsolved, so it is 0.0. A "pass" or "not graded" rubric verdict never lowers the score.
    """
    f, t = int(f2p_passed), int(f2p_total)
    p, q = int(p2p_passed), int(p2p_total)
    solved = bool(t) and f == t and p == q
    tests_passed = 1.0 if solved else 0.0
    _canon.clear()
    _canon.update({
        'reward': 0.0 if rubric == 'fail' else tests_passed,
        'tests_passed': tests_passed,
        'f2p_passed': f, 'f2p_total': t,
        'p2p_passed': p, 'p2p_total': q,
        'rubric_passed': {'pass': 1, 'fail': 0}.get(rubric, -1),
    })
    return _canon['reward']


@atexit.register
def _canon_flush():
    if not _canon:
        return
    try:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(_CANON_JSON), exist_ok=True)
        with open(_CANON_JSON, 'w') as fh:
            json.dump(_canon, fh, indent=2)
        # reward.txt too: harbor prefers reward.json, but the sandbox teardown script and
        # the lighthouse UI read reward.txt. One dict writes both, so they cannot disagree.
        with open(_CANON_TXT, 'w') as fh:
            fh.write(str(_canon['reward']))
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"WARNING: could not write {_CANON_JSON}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)


def rubric_verdict(argv):
    """The verdict test.sh hands in as `--rubric pass|fail|""`.

    Anything that is not an explicit pass/fail — including the empty string test.sh passes
    when no rubric shipped — means "not graded", which must never penalise the run.
    """
    if '--rubric' not in argv:
        return None
    i = argv.index('--rubric')
    value = argv[i + 1].strip().lower() if i + 1 < len(argv) else ''
    return value if value in ('pass', 'fail') else None



def load_results():
    """Return {combined_id: 'pass'|'fail'|'skip'} from the JUnit XML."""
    results = {}
    if not os.path.exists(REPORT):
        return results
    try:
        tree = ET.parse(REPORT)
    except ET.ParseError as exc:
        print(f"[verifier] WARNING: could not parse {REPORT}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return results
    for tc in tree.iter('testcase'):
        # Vitest JUnit: classname = describe block(s), name = test title.
        # We combine them so substring matching catches both long and short forms.
        classname = tc.get('classname', '')
        name      = tc.get('name', '')
        combined  = f"{classname}::{name}".strip(':')
        failed    = any(c.tag in ('failure', 'error') for c in tc)
        skipped   = any(c.tag == 'skipped'            for c in tc)
        results[combined] = 'skip' if skipped else ('fail' if failed else 'pass')
    return results


def matched(idents, results):
    """Return {ident: 'pass'|'fail'|'skip'|'missing'}.
    Matching is substring-first, regex-fallback, to tolerate minor name changes."""
    out = {}
    for ident in idents:
        hit = next(
            (v for k, v in results.items()
             if ident in k or re.search(re.escape(ident), k)),
            None,
        )
        out[ident] = hit if hit is not None else 'missing'
    return out


def main():
    r    = load_results()
    f2p  = matched(F2P, r)
    p2p  = matched(P2P, r)

    f2p_pass = [k for k, v in f2p.items() if v == 'pass']
    p2p_pass = [k for k, v in p2p.items() if v == 'pass']

    # Reward policy: BINARY — 1.0 only if every f2p flipped AND every p2p still passes.
    # Anything less is 0.0; the counts below carry how close the run got.
    reward = canon_reward(len(f2p_pass), len(F2P),
                          len(p2p_pass), len(P2P),
                          rubric_verdict(sys.argv[1:]))

    print(json.dumps({
        'reward': reward,
        'f2p':    f2p,
        'p2p':    p2p,
        'f2p_pass_count': len(f2p_pass),
        'f2p_total':      len(F2P),
        'p2p_pass_count': len(p2p_pass),
        'p2p_total':      len(P2P),
    }, indent=2))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
